text: BST order; set for predecessor and successor.

A binary search tree (BST, 二叉搜索树) keeps smaller keys in the left subtree and larger in the right, so search, insert and delete follow one root-to-leaf path. A balanced tree (平衡树) keeps that path O(log n) however the keys arrive; a plain BST fed 1, 2, 3, … becomes a chain.

Try the STL first: set / multiset / map are balanced trees (red-black) with insert, erase, lower_bound, predecessor and successor in O(log n). Write your own tree only when you need ranks, k-th element, or operations on whole ranges of a sequence.
Turnover (P2234): each day adds the smallest difference to any earlier value. The closest earlier values are the successor (lower_bound) and the predecessor (the element before it) in a sorted set.

Random priorities; split and merge; six operations.
split(root, 4): green tree ≤ 4, blue tree > 4 only the dashed edge is cut

The FHQ Treap (无旋 Treap) gives each node a random priority and keeps keys in BST order and priorities in heap order. Random priorities make the expected depth O(log n). Everything is built from two operations: split(t, k) cuts t into keys ≤ k and keys > k; merge(a, b) joins two trees where every key of a is ≤ every key of b.

Insert x: split at x, merge(merge(left, new node), right). Delete one x: split into < x, = x, > x; drop one node from the middle (merge its children); merge back. Rank, k-th, predecessor and successor all follow from split plus subtree sizes.
45 else { split(root, x, a, b); cout << kth(b, 1) << "\n"; root = merge(a, b); }
47 return 0;

The six operations of the normal balanced tree (P3369): insert, delete one, rank of x (how many are smaller, + 1), k-th smallest, predecessor (largest < x), successor (smallest > x). Every split is followed by a merge that puts the tree back together.
Call up() after every change of children, inside both split and merge. When deleting, split at x and at x − 1 so the middle tree holds only copies of x, and remove just its root.
Implicit keys; lazy reversal; maintaining a sequence.

Implicit keys (按大小分裂): store a sequence in the tree, ordered by position instead of by value. split(t, k) now gives the first k elements and the rest, using subtree sizes. A range [l, r] is cut out with two splits, changed as one subtree, and glued back with two merges.

Range updates use lazy tags, as in segment trees (第6章). To reverse a range, set a flag on the subtree root; when the node is visited later, swap its children and pass the flag down (P3391). Insert and delete inside the sequence are just more splits and merges.
Reversals: 12345 → 32145 → 12345 → 43215. Each reversal is two splits, one flag and two merges: O(log n) expected, however long the range.

Splay trees (伸展树) do the same jobs by rotating the accessed node to the root; they are needed for link- cut trees but are harder to write. For contest use, FHQ Treap covers almost everything a balanced tree is needed for, including "maintain a sequence" (P2042 维护数列 , P4008 文本编辑器).

Other ways to get ranks without writing a tree: a Fenwick tree over discretised values when all values are known in advance (第5章), or __gnu_pbds::tree with order_of_key / find_by_order when the judge allows it. Merging many small sets into large ones (永无乡 P3224) uses small-to-large merging of treaps.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. STL set / multiset / map first; own tree for ranks, k-th, or sequences.
2. Treap: BST by key, heap by random priority ⇒ expected depth O(log n).
3. split(t, k): ≤ k and > k; merge(a, b) with keys of a ≤ keys of b.
4. Insert = split + merge; delete one = split at x and x − 1, merge the middle's children.
5. Rank = size of (< x) + 1; k-th by walking with subtree sizes.
6. Implicit key: split by size; range = two splits; lazy flags like segment trees.
7. Reverse: flag, and swap children when pushing down.
